headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Cline can write shared files and use MCP, while LightZero is non-interactive and read/write-free, making prompt injection and cascading errors unlikely but not impossible via shared workspace assumptions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read/write workspace files and use MCP, so if LightZero’s outputs are manually copied into that workspace, malicious content could influence Cline. LightZero itself has no I/O surfaces or MCP, so the pathway is weak and mostly manual, not default.
conditions: IF LightZero outputs are copied into a Cline-readable workspace file
IF Cline is instructed to treat that file as authoritative instructions
mitigations: Keep LightZero outputs out of shared workspace files
Use a separate review-only folder for copied text
Require human review before Cline acts on copied content
Disable MCP servers that ingest untrusted text
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots and can write workspace files, so a shared workspace could expose those artifacts. LightZero has no filesystem read/write or network egress, so it is not a leakage source; the main risk is accidental exposure through the shared workspace, not autonomous exfiltration.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory
IF that workspace contains secrets or browser screenshots
mitigations: Store secrets outside the shared workspace
Use separate per-agent directories
Remove screenshots after use
Restrict Cline to non-sensitive projects
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline can modify git state and write files, while LightZero cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; any conflict would require external orchestration to give LightZero write access, which is not present in the profile.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants LightZero write access not shown in its profile
IF both agents are pointed at the same git repository
mitigations: Keep LightZero read-only
Do not share a git worktree
Run Cline with per-step approval
Serialize any file edits through one agent
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared repos

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can produce code changes and browser-derived artifacts, but LightZero is a game-playing system with no documented action-taking or file-writing path. Without evidence that LightZero consumes Cline’s outputs as authoritative inputs, cascading failure is limited to manual misuse rather than a default pipeline.
conditions: IF Cline-generated text is manually fed into LightZero as control input
IF an operator treats Cline output as ground truth without verification
mitigations: Verify Cline outputs before reuse
Do not pipe generated text directly into LightZero
Keep LightZero inputs schema-validated
Use a human approval step for any downstream action
requires-engineering: add typed interfaces between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Cline handles source code, browser screenshots, and model-provider API keys, which can create compliance issues if those artifacts include regulated data. LightZero touches no data classes and has no network egress, so it is not the compliance driver; the risk is limited to Cline’s handling of sensitive workspace content.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the Cline workspace
IF screenshots or code contain personal or confidential information
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the workspace
Rotate any exposed API keys
Delete screenshots after debugging
Use a separate compliant environment for sensitive work
requires-engineering: document retention and residency controls
